title: Transfers of the Whole Available Balance to a Linked Bank — Pocketwire Personal Account
content:
Customers of the Pocketwire Personal Account may ask to move everything they can out of the personal balance to their linked bank. Such a transfer goes by standard transfer to the linked bank account and carries the available transfer amount of the account.

### Prerequisite

A transfer of the whole available balance is not sized until the account carries a plan fee entry for every billing period whose renewal date has arrived.

Put the other way round: as long as any billing period whose renewal date has arrived has no plan fee entry on the account, the whole available balance has no size yet.

### Cash-out rules

The cash-out rules of the personal account still apply to the transfer: the account must be active or closure pending, the day's cash-outs together may not exceed the plan's daily cash-out limit, and no cash-out may exceed the ledger balance.

### The customer's own transfer — `transfer_balance_to_bank_3181bc35`

**What it does.** With this tool the customer sends money from their own Pocketwire personal balance to their linked bank account by standard (free) transfer. One call books one standard cash-out dated today for the amount given to the bank account ending in the four digits given and takes that amount off the account's ledger balance; the transfer then shows in the app activity as a standard transfer on its way to the bank. No fee is charged on a standard transfer.

**How it is invoked.** It is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `transfer_balance_to_bank_3181bc35` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. The call books the amount supplied; it does not work out an amount.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `wallet_id` | The reference number of the customer's personal account the money leaves, as returned by the personal account lookup and given to the customer by the representative | Id |
| `amount` | The amount to send to the bank | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places |
| `destination_last4` | The last four digits of the linked bank account that receives the transfer | Exactly 4 digits, as the customer reads them from their bank details |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the transfer reference number, the amount sent in USD with 2 decimal places, the last four digits of the receiving bank account, and the ledger balance in USD left on the personal account. A receipt that names the transfer reference number means the standard transfer is booked.
